name: Vintage Photo Collage
visualIdentity: An explicitly sourced vintage collage: period-consistent photographs, newspaper fragments, clipped objects, visible paper edges, and distinct grain and print qualities unified by tone.
suitableUses: Useful for historical documentaries, archives, editorial introductions, and explanatory narratives. This is inferred suitability; the source explicitly recommends archival labels or timeline structures for historical material, including video and interactive HTML.
limitations: Requires period photographs; none are supplied in the source. Do not invent photos, cover faces with labels, overcrowd, fabricate timeline data, or add excessive parallax. Use the chapter motions only when they clarify the story; short topics or continuous-shot requirements may not suit chapter transitions.
palette: No canonical palette is specified. Preserve source-photo colors and grain, task or brand colors, and existing role assignments. Optional fallback tokens for new presentation elements only: paper background #EDE3CD, type #393329, subordinate accent #85765D. Use discrete colors, no gradient; the accent fails normal-text contrast on the paper background, so reserve it for decoration. Recheck actual compositing.
motionAndInteraction: Animate cutouts, object-based scene links, and modest parallax. For video, derive motion from seekable composition time. For HTML, chapter/story progress may follow scroll with reversible states and readable holds; timeline navigation should be keyboard-accessible. A gallery pattern is suitable only with actual images and captions, and should keep selection and caption synchronized. Keep motion restrained and avoid excessive depth.
audio: Unspecified; choose music, narration, effects, ambience, or silence for the topic and audience. Honor supplied audio requirements and assets, then synchronize and mix with picture; do not assume a soundtrack.
assetRequirements: Prepare period-consistent photographs, newspaper fragments, clipped objects, transparent cutouts, visible paper edges, and print textures. Match tones while retaining each image's grain and print character. Crop authoring may frame images but does not extract subjects or create missing parallax layers. Interactive galleries need accurate image dimensions and responsive sources.
combinations: Style-024 archival labels can add contextual handwritten notes; keep them #393329, neutral, and off faces. Style-097 timelines or maps can organize accurate historical events; use paper strips and consistent texture. These combinations are suggestions, not requirements.
productionApproach: Use a style-specific renderer such as optional PixiJS for layered 2D artwork and masks, with GSAP for deterministic movement when needed. Python/Pillow can prepare cutouts, crops, and textures. HyperFrames owns composition timing, media/audio sync, checks, and export; use Remotion only if HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a required capability. For HTML lightboxes, PhotoSwipe is optional and does not create collage artwork.
